caption: Forex Desk
vo: Foreign exchange moves fast. Let's follow Genesis Forex from a client's FX profile to a booked deal, through quotes, forwards and rate alerts.

caption: Le Morne Resorts Ltd, a hotel group, earns euros and pays its costs in rupees
vo: Le Morne Resorts is a hotel group. It earns euros but pays its costs in rupees, so it wants to sell those euros forward. First, an FX profile.

caption: Sign in as Deepak Mungur — Forex Dealer
vo: We're Deepak Mungur, the forex dealer, who quotes, books deals, and looks after forwards and alerts.

caption: Forex Desk ▸ FX Client Profiles: one profile per FX client
vo: Every FX client gets one profile. Its purpose, volumes, currency pairs, approved products and limits.

caption: “Forex client onboarding” opens a two-step wizard
vo: Forex client onboarding walks Deepak through it in two steps. First the client's FX need, then the products and limits.

caption: Approved products and the settlement limit
vo: Here are the approved products and the settlement limit. The limit is checked against open forwards, and the utilisation is worked out for you.

caption: Profile created
vo: And the profile's created. Deals, open forwards and limit usage will build up right here.

caption: The client calls: sell EUR 300,000 forward, in six weeks
vo: Now the client calls. It wants to sell three hundred thousand euros forward, in six weeks. Deepak opens a new FX quote with the client, profile, product, side, currency and amount.

caption: “Requested at” is stamped with the time of the call
vo: Requested at is stamped with the time of the call. That's where the quote timer starts.

caption: The FX quote timer: answer within 15 business minutes
vo: Why a timer? Best execution. Deepak has fifteen business minutes to answer, and since it counts business hours only, a weekend request is due Monday.

caption: FX Quotes on the pipeline board
vo: Here's the quote on the board. Requested, quoted, then accepted, rejected or expired.

caption: Move the quote to Quoted…
vo: Let's move it to Quoted before entering a rate.

caption: Blocked: a quote needs the quoted rate and the time it was given
vo: Blocked. A quote needs its rate and the time it was given. No rate, no quote.

caption: The board buys EUR at 52.64 — Deepak quotes the client 52.90
vo: The board buys euros at fifty-two point six four. Deepak quotes the client fifty-two point nine zero, and enters the rate with the time it was given.

caption: Quoted — the first-response timer is met
vo: Quoted, and the first-response timer is met. The improvement on the board rate is calculated on the quote.

caption: The client agrees to the rate
vo: The client agrees, so Deepak moves it to Accepted.

caption: Blocked: record when the client responded
vo: Blocked again, and for a good reason. The CRM wants to know when the client responded. That completes the time-stamped trail, from requested, to quoted, to the client's answer. If anyone ever asks how this deal was priced, it's all there.

caption: Accepted: the CRM books the deal for you
vo: Accepted. And the CRM books the deal for Deepak, sending it straight to the dealing system.

caption: Forex Desk ▸ FX Deals: the deal booked from the quote
vo: Here it is in FX Deals, booked from the quote. A forward, three hundred thousand euros at fifty-two point nine zero.

caption: The dealing system's reference is recorded on the deal
vo: The dealing system's reference is already on the deal, recorded when it was booked.

caption: Board rate 52.64 · quoted 52.90 — the client gets MUR 78,000 more
vo: Here's what it means for the client. Board rate fifty-two point six four, quoted fifty-two point nine zero, so seventy-eight thousand rupees more. That's best-execution evidence.

caption: An open forward until it settles
vo: Until it settles, it's an open forward. The days to value date count down, and it counts against the limit.

caption: Reminders tab: the CRM reminds the dealer a week before the value date
vo: And nobody has to remember the date. A week before, the CRM reminds Deepak to confirm settlement or offer a roll-over.

caption: On that day the client is also emailed and a roll-over offered
vo: On the day, the client is emailed a roll-over offer. The date's in Deepak's calendar feed too.

caption: The client also wants to sell more euros if EUR/MUR rises to 53.60
vo: One more request. If the euro rises to fifty-three point six zero against the rupee, the client wants to sell more. So Deepak sets a rate alert, and the client's emailed when the board gets there.

caption: Active: today's board is 53.43 — below the target
vo: It's active. Today's board is fifty-three point four three, below target. Alerts are checked hourly, and whenever a new board rate is published.

caption: Next morning's board: the euro is stronger
vo: Next morning, the euro is stronger. Deepak publishes the new TT buying and selling rates in FX Reference Rates.

caption: The board feeds every MUR conversion, the rate alerts and the website
vo: That board feeds every rupee conversion, the rate alerts, and the website.

caption: 53.65 is above the client's 53.60 — the alert fires at once
vo: Fifty-three point six five is above the client's fifty-three point six zero, so the alert fires at once. The client's emailed, the alert closes as triggered, and Deepak's notified.

caption: The email to the client is on the alert's timeline
vo: The email's right there on the alert's timeline, in French, the client's language. It goes by SMS when the client prefers.

caption: Deepak is notified to call the client and deal
vo: And the bell tells Deepak to call the client and deal.

caption: The Forex Desk dashboard
vo: All of this rolls into the Forex Desk dashboard. Deals, volume, spread income, and the forwards still open.

caption: Volume by currency and by month, top clients
vo: Volume by currency and by month, the top clients, quote outcomes, and rate alerts.

caption: Forex Desk
vo: So that's the Forex Desk. The dealer quotes and decides, and the CRM keeps the trail, books the deal and sends the reminders. Next up, Marketing and Consent.
